primary_claim: Bradley-Terry value rankings fit on Zhang et al.'s (2025) LLM values dataset predict out-of-sample pairwise value comparisons better than chance (62.4% for o4-mini to 88.1% for Grok-4) and are correlated with independent multi-turn Petri auditor evaluations for models with high out-of-sample accuracy, but rephrasing borderline-refusable queries to embody a model's own highly-ranked values generally fails to reduce its refusal rate

effect.metric: out-of-sample pairwise prediction accuracy (BT model); refusal rate under value-laden query rephrasing
effect.value: accuracy 62.4% (o4-mini) to 88.1% (Grok-4), chance=50%; value-laden rephrasing has no significant effect on aggregate refusal rate across models (one marginal exception: Grok-4 on Claude-generated questions, p=0.02)

stated_future_work: Put more effort into aggregating values to those most salient to a model to yield rankings with better predictive power
Directly test tradeoffs with safety-related values in Petri
Further investigate how current LLMs trade off between non-safety-related values in nontrivial multi-turn situations
Explore the exact algorithms or thought processes models use to decide value tradeoffs
limitations_stated: Small sample sizes: Petri validation uses only 20 value pairs, refusal experiment uses only 10 handwritten questions plus generated variants
Bradley-Terry model assumes transitivity and context-independence of preferences, which may not hold for LLM values that could be highly context-dependent
Some models (o3, GPT-4o) show weaker out-of-sample predictability (62.6%, 63.9%)
Author explicitly frames this as an interim, lightly-explored research note with limited conclusive progress
The marginal Grok-4 refusal effect could be due to statistical noise (p=0.02)
quote: We find that these value rankings are meaningfully predictive in some models: they can predict out-of-sample pairwise comparisons with accuracy ranging from 62.4% (o4-mini) to 88.1% (Grok-4), where chance is 50%... directly paraphrasing chat queries that are borderline-refused to embody a model's preferred values generally has no effect on whether the model refuses the query.
